generation.prompt: The reference image is a style and camera reference only. Match its ink line weight, woodcut hatching, cream parchment fill, three-quarter top-down camera angle, and sprite scale exactly, but draw a completely different subject; do not copy the reference creature. Subject: an elite gilded beast: a stocky lion-headed marginalia grotesque on four clawed legs with a curling tail and a spiky mane, prowling forward, snarling. Style: a medieval manuscript marginalia drollery drawn as a bold woodcut print. Thick, confident black ink outlines, simplified chunky shapes, a little bold black hatching for shadow only, no fine cross-hatching. Palette black ink on warm cream parchment fills, with large areas of burnished gold leaf on the mane, back and tail (gold marks it as an elite); no other colors. Camera: a single isolated game sprite seen in three-quarter top-down view, camera above and in front looking down at 45 degrees. Whole body fully visible with empty margin on all sides, centered, facing right, in profile-three-quarter. No ground, no cast shadow, no text, no frame, transparent background.
